delightkitr

Small, purposeless decorative flourishes for R, drawn from geometry alone. Every ornament takes a seed, so the same seed always gives the same flourish and a new one gives a new sibling.

Swelled rule

A line that thickens and tapers like a pen stroke, finished with dot, diamond or fleuron endcaps.

Fleuron rule

A centred fleuron with tapering rules and a few beads strung along each side.

Pen swash

An S-shaped copperplate flourish that swells in the middle and curls at both ends.

Rinceau

A running scroll: a wavy stem with a spiral curl at every crest and trough.

Greek key

The square meander: one continuous line winding into a rectangular spiral, tile after tile.

Scallop border

A row of arches, each with a smaller arch inside and a bead where neighbours meet.

Compass rose

A star of long and short rays with two-tone shading, a tick ring and a north marker.

Guilloche

The woven engraved rosette of banknotes: many wavy circles, each rotated a little.

Petal rosette

A flower-like medallion of alternating petal layers around a jewelled centre.

Sunburst

Alternating long and short rays around a ringed hub, in the Art Deco manner.

Corner flourish

A bracket for the corner of a page or frame, ending in inward-turning curls.

Dinkus / asterism

The small break between sections: three stars in a row, or in a triangle.

In ggplot2 and gt

Frame a whole plot, border just its panel, or dress a table: border ornaments fit themselves to each side.

Generated by data-raw/build-gallery.R with the package’s own ornament_svg().
github.com/DavidBrocker/delightkitr

Design principle — small ornament kinds generated from geometry with seeded variation — follows tikz-flora by wn-mitch (MIT). The shapes here are independently written in R.
